chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id from Safwan ibn Yahya and Fadalah from al-Ala' ibn Razeen from Muhammad ibn Muslim from one of them (peace be upon them) said:
«It is not appropriate for the Imam to pray Dhuhr on the Day of Tarwiyah except in Mina, and he should spend the night there until sunrise.».

key_terms.اَلتَّرْوِيَةِ: The Day of Tarwiyah, the 8th of Dhu al-Hijjah, marking the beginning of the core Hajj rituals.
key_terms.بِمِنًى: In Mina, the plain near Mecca where pilgrims spend the nights of the Hajj days.
key_terms.طُلُوعِ اَلشَّمْسِ: Sunrise, the time marking the end of the night stay in Mina for this specific ruling.

ai.seo_question: Where and when should the Imam pray Dhuhr on the Day of Tarwiyah according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* underscores the distinct legal status of the Imam (or Caliph) during Hajj, mandating that on the Day of Tarwiyah, he must perform Dhuhr prayer in Mina and remain there overnight until sunrise, distinguishing his practice from that of the general populace. This ruling highlights the Imam's role as the leader of the pilgrimage rites, ensuring the proper execution of rituals in their designated locations as part of the Sunnah. The emphasis on Mina reflects the historical and spiritual significance of this valley as the site of preparation and sacrifice before proceeding to Arafat.
